name: Modern Horizons 2
credit: Archetypes from Mark Rosewater's Modern Horizons 2 design article (Wizards of the Coast). Wizards named no signposts; the ones here are the set's gold uncommons, which player guides treat as each pair's signature card. Notes and key cards from Flipside Gaming's and Draftsim's guides, reworded.
about: The archetypes overlap a lot: artifacts, graveyard, big mana, tokens and +1/+1 counters each run through several pairs. Fixing is strong (the artifact dual lands, Ornithopter of Paradise, Rift Sower, the landcyclers), so three-color and even five-color decks happen. Removal is efficient; Tragic Fall, Bone Shards and Unholy Heat are the commons players name most.

src.t: Modern Approach, Part 2 (Wizards of the Coast)
A Limited Guide to Modern Horizons 2 (Flipside Gaming)

list.d: Affinity and metalcraft: get artifacts down early, find more, then cast affinity cards far ahead of schedule.
list.p: Count your artifacts a few turns ahead so Sojourner's Companion and Steelfin Whale come down cheap.

list.d: Cards that reward you for discarding from your own hand. Works well alongside reanimation, delirium and madness.
list.p: Keep a steady supply of discard outlets; the payoffs shine in long games.

list.d: Empty your hand fast and use discard-as-a-cost cards to cast madness spells cheaply.
list.p: Use a discard outlet to flash Hell Mongrel in at the end of the opponent's turn.

list.d: Cast many spells in one turn and get paid for each.
list.p: The least supported pair: ramp on its own is not enough, you need turns with several spells.

list.d: The most traditional plan in the set: play creatures, grow them, remove blockers and attack.
list.p: Hold Unbounded Potential and Captured by Lagacs until they add the most counters.

list.d: Put creatures in the graveyard and bring them back; big ones are the prize, small ones still bring value.
list.p: Against aggro, don't trade Breathless Knight away: its lifelink is how you stabilize.

list.d: Get four card types into your graveyard to unlock strong bonuses.
list.p: One of the harder decks to draft. Mix card types with self-mill and discard, and lean toward tempo rather than pure control.

list.d: Go wide with Squirrel tokens and sacrifice them for value.
list.p: Needs some luck to come together, but it is powerful when it does. Activate Vermin Gorger and Legion Vanguard on the opponent's turn, often alongside a chump block.

list.d: A more aggressive artifact deck built on modular: small artifact creatures that merge their counters.
list.p: Play lots of creatures and commit several early to outpace removal; modular moves counters from a blocked creature to an unblocked one.

list.d: Creature tokens plus Clues, Food and Treasure, for steady card advantage or a swarm of evasive attackers.
list.p: Don't chump block with your tokens early: Junk Winder and Combine Chrysalis want them.

list.d: Rosewater's extra archetype: use the set's fixing to play every color and power up converge cards.
